review_candidates.title: Sr. Mechatronics Engineer - Actuation & Drivetrain
review_candidates.description: Location : Onsite — Austin, TX Employment Type : Direct Hire, Full‑Time Job Title : Senior Mechatronics Engineer - Actuation & Drivetrain About 9 Mothers The modern battlefield has changed. Cheap, autonomous suicide drones have turned the tactical advantage upside down, and the world is looking for a solution. At 9 Mothers, we aren’t just "innovating"—we are building the shield. Backed by top-tier investors, we develop AI powered machines designed to intercept and neutralize Group 1/sUAS threats in real-time. Our flagship product is a low-power, counter-drone system built for the edge—on vehicles, at bases, or in a soldier's pack. Why 9 Mothers? While others build for "awareness" or "long-term research," we build for the immediate survival of those in harm’s way. We are a team of hackers, engineers, and mission-driven builders who value field-ready capability over polished slide decks. If you want to see your code or hardware in the field next month—not next year—this is your playground. Position Summary EDDA is only as good as its actuators, and we're hiring the person who owns them. You will be our servo wizard: the single owner of every motor, actuator, gearbox and solenoid in the product, from the first torque and inertia calculation through supplier selection, bench characterization, control-loop tuning, abuse testing and production release. You are as fluent in gearbox design — backlash, torsional stiffness, efficiency, lubrication, lifetime — as you are inside the current loop of the servo driving it. And you have lived with motion systems that get rained on, dropped, fired next to and bounced across a field on the back of a truck. What You'll Own Everything in the product that converts electrons into motion is yours — the parts, the suppliers, the test data and the tuning. Motors and actuators: BLDC/PMSM and frameless torque motors, steppers where they earn their place, linear actuators — every axis that moves EDDA's azimuth, elevation and auxiliary mechanisms. Gearboxes and drivetrain: planetary, strain-wave (harmonic), cycloidal, worm and belt stages; the direct-drive-versus-geared call on each axis; bearing arrangements, preload, backlash and the stiffness budget that sets achievable control bandwidth. Solenoids and discrete actuators: latches, safeties, indexing and release mechanisms — the fast, simple actuators that must work every time, in the cold, after being dropped. Motor drives and tuning: drive selection or specification, commutation and feedback (encoders, resolvers, Hall sensors), current/velocity/position loop tuning, feedforward and filtering. Characterization and test: dynamometer and bench rigs, thermal derating, torque ripple and cogging, efficiency maps, endurance and abuse testing, and the acceptance tests production runs on every unit. The actuation supply chain: vendor qualification, custom motor and gearbox specifications, second sources, cost-down and the lead times that production depends on. Essential Duties Size and select: turn slew-rate, acceleration, pointing-accuracy and duty-cycle requirements into torque, speed, reflected-inertia and thermal budgets; pick or specify the motor, gear ratio and drive that meet them with margin — and show the math. Design the drivetrain: own the mechanical path from rotor to load — gear stages, couplings, shafts, bearings, preload, lubrication and seals — and the stiffness and backlash budget that determines how hard the loops can be pushed. Characterize everything: build the rigs and run the tests — torque constant, back-EMF, inductance, cogging and ripple, friction and stiction, efficiency, thermal rise, backlash and lost motion — so tuning starts from a measured plant, not a datasheet. Tune the loops: commission and tune current, velocity and position loops (PID, feedforward, notch filters, observers) for aggressive high-bandwidth tracking without exciting structural modes or cooking the motor. Engineer for abuse: design and qualify actuation for shock and vibration from vehicle mounts and weapon firing, dust, mud, water, salt, EMI and temperature extremes; lead failure analysis when hardware comes back from the range broken, and make sure the next revision doesn't. Own the supply chain: qualify vendors, write motor, gearbox and solenoid specifications, manage second sources and lead times, and drive cost-down for production volumes. Bridge the teams: be the technical interface between mechanical, electrical, firmware and robotics on anything that moves; triage failures at the hardware-software boundary and call whether a problem is mechanical, electrical or control. Document and release: derating curves, tuning procedures, acceptance tests and drawings that production and field teams can execute without you in the room. Requirements Experience: 10+ years in mechatronics or motion-system engineering with a track record of shipping servo-driven products — ideally pan-tilt units, gimbals, turrets, robotic joints or vehicle-mounted systems. Servo depth: hands-on selection, commissioning and tuning of BLDC/PMSM servo systems: field-oriented control, current/velocity/position loops, encoder and resolver feedback, drive configuration, and diagnosing instability, resonance and thermal limits on the bench. Gearbox fluency: working command of planetary, strain-wave, cycloidal and worm drives — ratio selection, efficiency, backlash, torsional stiffness, lubrication and lifetime — and a clear sense of when direct drive beats gearing. Actuator characterization: you have built test rigs and run dynamometer, thermal, efficiency and endurance tests; comfortable with scopes, current probes, DAQ and Python or MATLAB to extract plant parameters from data. Drivetrain design: can design and detail the mechanical path from rotor to load — bearings, shafts, couplings, seals, preload — in CAD (SolidWorks or similar) with tolerance analysis. Programming: enough C/C++ or Python to configure drives, automate tests and prototype control code; comfortable reading motor-control firmware. Supplier management: have specified custom motors or gearboxes with vendors and run qualification, second-sourcing and cost-down. Hands-on rigor: you build, break, measure and fix your own hardware. Compliance: U.S. citizenship and the ability to pass a background check. Nice‑to‑Have Harsh-environment qualification: MIL-STD-810 shock and vibration, IP-rated sealing, EMI/EMC, thermal cycling — and the scars from hardware that was abused in the field anyway. Weapon-mounted, recoil-loaded or vehicle-mounted motion systems. Custom motor design: frameless, outer-rotor or slotless motors and magnetics; electromagnetic FEA (Ansys Maxwell, JMAG, FEMM). Solenoid and voice-coil design: force-stroke-thermal trade-offs, PWM hold, fast actuation. Structural dynamics: modal analysis and designing control around structural modes; stabilization on a moving platform. Advanced control: model-predictive, adaptive or disturbance-observer control. Drive ecosystems: CAN, EtherCAT, ROS 2/DDS; hands-on time with ODrive, moteus, Elmo, Copley, Kollmorgen or similar drives. Production experience: DFM, incoming inspection and acceptance-test procedures for actuators. Security clearance or the ability to obtain one. You build robots, race drones or rebuild machinery on your own time. Benefits Meaningful Early Equity: You aren't just an employee; you are a foundational owner. Your contributions directly drive the value of your stake in the company. Direct Roadmap Influence: Forget the bureaucracy of big defense. You will have a seat at the table, directly shaping our product and technology trajectory from day one. Mission-Critical Work: We don't build for "what if." We build systems the Department of War actively needs to counter immediate, real-world threats. The Builder's Playground: Work in a brand-new lab fully optimized for rapid prototyping, equipped with NVIDIA Jetsons, high-end scopes, and 3-D printers. 100% Employer-Paid Premiums: We cover 100% of your medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums and cover 50% of healthcare premiums for your dependents. Unlimited PTO: We value results, not clock-watching. Take the time you need to stay sharp and recharge. Zero Red Tape: You report to the founders. You have the autonomy to make technical decisions that would take months of committee approval at a larger firm. Austin-Based Culture: Join an onsite team in Austin, TX, where we prioritize high-bandwidth collaboration and rapid field-testing. Relocation Assistance: We want the best talent in the room. If you aren't in Austin yet, we’ll help you get here, to make your transition to the Silicon Hills seamless. About The Interview Virtual interview (45 min via MS Teams) Onsite interview in Austin (1.5 hr in-person) Compensation Range: $150K - $200K

review_candidates.description: About Us Hydrafacial is a global category-creating company focused on bringing innovative products to market and delivering beauty health experiences by reinventing our consumer’s relationship with their skin, their bodies and their self-confidence. Every person here is a key player in our success. We are firm believers in making the little things count each day so the big things will follow. If this sounds like you, come check us out! This is the perfect opportunity to work with some of the best leaders in the industry while you gain the global and strategic experience to add to your professional toolbox. Job Description: WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS The Senior Manager, Training & Education – Mexico and LATAM Distributors leads the Training & Education strategy for Mexico and provides functional leadership and governance for assigned LATAM distributors. This role translates global learning strategies into locally relevant, scalable, and measurable education programs that support compliant product use, customer adoption, commercial capability, product launch readiness, and business growth. The position leads the Mexico Training & Education function, manages the operating plan and budget, establishes trainer and distributor capability standards, and serves as the primary strategic partner to Commercial, Marketing, Global Learning & Development, and cross-functional stakeholders. The role also drives training quality, operational excellence, and continuous improvement while supporting strategic customer engagement and business priorities across Mexico and assigned LATAM distributors. What You’ll Do Lead the annual Training & Education strategy and operating plan for Mexico and assigned LATAM distributors, aligning learning initiatives with commercial priorities, business objectives, and Global Learning & Development strategies. Translate business priorities and capability gaps into scalable, measurable education programs that support customer adoption, commercial effectiveness, product launch readiness, and business growth. Develop and execute an integrated portfolio of customer, commercial, product launch, and distributor education programs by partnering with Commercial, Marketing, Medical, Regulatory, Quality, Legal, Global Learning & Development, Key Opinion Leaders, strategic customers, and distributor partners to deliver high-impact learning solutions. Manage the Training & Education team, including leadership of the Regional Training Specialist (RTS), while establishing trainer onboarding, certification, calibration, and recertification standards. Provide functional leadership and development support to internal trainers and distributor training partners across the region. Lead customer and commercial education initiatives across Mexico by driving onboarding, competency development, coaching, product launch readiness, and ongoing capability-building programs that strengthen commercial performance and customer outcomes. Oversee distributor capability development across assigned LATAM markets by assessing learning needs, implementing train-the-trainer programs, supporting trainer certification, adapting education programs to local market and regulatory requirements, and ensuring consistent regional training standards. Ensure all training content, materials, and delivery comply with applicable regulatory requirements, approved product labelling, company policies, quality standards, and clinical governance requirements. Maintain audit-ready training documentation, certification records, competency assessments, and learning materials while supporting inspection readiness and appropriate escalation of product complaints, adverse events, safety observations, and other reportable issues. Manage the Training & Education budget, vendor relationships, contracts, and operational resources while overseeing Mexico Experience Center operations, training logistics, scheduling, facilities, inventory, and other activities that enable exceptional customer and commercial learning experiences. Measure training effectiveness through performance metrics, governance reporting, and business insights, identifying opportunities and implementing continuous improvement initiatives that enhance organizational capability and business performance. Perform other duties as assigned. Required WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. 7+ years of progressive experience in Training & Education, Clinical Education, Commercial Excellence, or Learning & Development, preferably within the medical device, aesthetics, healthcare, or another regulated industry. 2+ years of direct people leadership experience, including performance management, coaching, and talent development. Demonstrated experience developing and executing annual operating plans, cross-functional learning strategies, capability frameworks, assessments, and measurable learning outcomes. Experience delivering high-impact in-person and virtual education to customers, healthcare or aesthetic professionals, and commercial teams. Working knowledge of instructional design principles, adult learning methodologies, learning management systems (LMS), and train-the-trainer models. Fluent professional proficiency in English and Spanish, both written and spoken. Ability to travel approximately 50%, primarily within Mexico. Preferred Experience working across multiple countries and supporting distributor or indirect commercial business models. Experience managing budgets, forecasts, vendors, facilitator relationships, and service contracts. Experience supporting Quality, Regulatory, and complaint/adverse event escalation processes within a regulated medical device environment. Professional certification in clinical education, aesthetics, instructional design, project management, or a related discipline. Portuguese language proficiency or experience supporting Portuguese-language training resources. Physical Requirements Of The Job Field- and office-based role requiring approximately 50% travel, including multi-day domestic and occasional international travel. Valid driver's license and reliable personal transportation. Ability to stand, walk, and work in clinical environments for extended periods of up to eight hours. Ability to lift and carry training materials, demonstration equipment, and supplies weighing up to 30 pounds. Ability to demonstrate company products and procedures during customer education and training activities, as required. Ability to sit for extended periods while traveling or working on a computer. Ability to set up and dismantle training and demonstration equipment for customer events, trade shows, and company meetings, as required. POR QUÉ ESTE PUESTO ES IMPORTANTE El/la Senior Manager, Training & Education – Mexico and LATAM Distributors lidera la estrategia de Training & Education para México y proporciona liderazgo funcional y gobernanza para los distribuidores asignados en LATAM. Esta posición traduce las estrategias globales de aprendizaje en programas de educación y capacitación relevantes para el mercado local, escalables y medibles, que promueven el uso adecuado y conforme de los productos, la adopción por parte de los clientes, el desarrollo de capacidades comerciales, la preparación para lanzamientos de productos y el crecimiento del negocio. Esta posición lidera la función de Training & Education en México, administra el plan operativo y el presupuesto, establece estándares de capacitación y desarrollo de capacidades para trainers y distribuidores, y actúa como socio estratégico principal de Commercial, Marketing, Global Learning & Development y otras áreas clave de la organización. Asimismo, impulsa la calidad de la capacitación, la excelencia operativa y la mejora continua, a la vez que apoya la relación con clientes estratégicos y las prioridades del negocio en México y los distribuidores asignados en LATAM. QUÉ HARÁS Liderar la estrategia anual y el plan operativo de Training & Education para México y los distribuidores asignados en LATAM, alineando las iniciativas de aprendizaje con las prioridades comerciales, los objetivos del negocio y las estrategias de Global Learning & Development. Traducir las prioridades del negocio y las brechas de capacidades en programas de educación y capacitación escalables y medibles que impulsen la adopción por parte de los clientes, la efectividad comercial, la preparación para lanzamientos de productos y el crecimiento del negocio. Desarrollar y ejecutar un portafolio integral de programas de educación y capacitación para clientes, equipos comerciales, lanzamientos de productos y distribuidores, en colaboración con Commercial, Marketing, Medical, Regulatory, Quality, Legal, Global Learning & Development, Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), clientes estratégicos y socios distribuidores, con el objetivo de ofrecer soluciones de aprendizaje de alto impacto. Gestionar al equipo de Training & Education, incluyendo el liderazgo del Regional Training Specialist (RTS), estableciendo estándares de onboarding, certificación, calibración y recertificación para trainers. Proporcionar liderazgo funcional y apoyo para el desarrollo de trainers internos y socios de capacitación de distribuidores en toda la región. Liderar las iniciativas de educación para clientes y equipos comerciales en México, impulsando el onboarding, el desarrollo de competencias, el coaching, la preparación para lanzamientos de productos y los programas continuos de desarrollo de capacidades que fortalezcan el desempeño comercial y los resultados de los clientes. Supervisar el desarrollo de capacidades de los distribuidores en los mercados asignados de LATAM mediante la evaluación de necesidades de aprendizaje, la implementación de programas train-the-trainer, el apoyo a la certificación de trainers, la adaptación de los programas de educación y capacitación a las necesidades del mercado local y a los requisitos regulatorios aplicables, y el aseguramiento de estándares de capacitación consistentes en toda la región. Garantizar que todo el contenido, los materiales y la impartición de las capacitaciones cumplan con los requisitos regulatorios aplicables, el etiquetado aprobado de los productos, las políticas de la compañía, los estándares de calidad y los requisitos de gobernanza clínica. Mantener la documentación de capacitación, los registros de certificación, las evaluaciones de competencias y los materiales de aprendizaje debidamente actualizados y preparados para auditorías; apoyar la preparación para inspecciones y asegurar el escalamiento adecuado de quejas de producto, eventos adversos, observaciones de seguridad y cualquier otro asunto sujeto a reporte. Administrar el presupuesto de Training & Education, las relaciones con proveedores, contratos y recursos operativos, así como supervisar las operaciones del Experience Center de México, incluyendo la logística de capacitación, programación, instalaciones, inventario y demás actividades necesarias para brindar experiencias excepcionales de aprendizaje a clientes y equipos comerciales. Medir la efectividad de los programas de capacitación mediante indicadores de desempeño, reportes de gobernanza e insights del negocio, identificando oportunidades e implementando iniciativas de mejora continua que fortalezcan las capacidades de la organización y el desempeño del negocio. Realizar otras funciones que le sean asignadas. LO QUE BUSCAMOS Requisitos Licenciatura concluida o una combinación equivalente de formación académica y experiencia relevante. Más de 7 años de experiencia progresiva en Training & Education, Clinical Education, Commercial Excellence o Learning & Development, preferentemente dentro de la industria de dispositivos médicos, estética, salud u otra industria regulada. Más de 2 años de experiencia directa liderando equipos, incluyendo gestión del desempeño, coaching y desarrollo de talento. Experiencia comprobada en el desarrollo y ejecución de planes operativos anuales, estrategias de aprendizaje multifuncionales, marcos de desarrollo de capacidades, evaluaciones y resultados de aprendizaje medibles. Experiencia impartiendo programas de educación y capacitación presenciales y virtuales de alto impacto para clientes, profesionales de la salud o de la estética y equipos comerciales. Conocimiento práctico de principios de diseño instruccional, metodologías de aprendizaje para adultos, sistemas de gestión del aprendizaje (LMS) y modelos train-the-trainer. Dominio profesional fluido del inglés y español, tanto oral como escrito. Disponibilidad para viajar aproximadamente el 50% del tiempo, principalmente dentro de México. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI. What is The Role: To support our continued growth and build a best in class Global Sales Compensation organisation, we are looking for a Principal Analyst Sales Compensation Systems & Administration to join our team! We will look to you to drive accuracy and efficiency in our sales compensation processes and reporting. Above all, this role will care and ensure our growing global sales organization, its leaders, have a best-in-call commissions process with white glove treatment while meeting Elastic’s scaling business needs as they change. If you are passionate about driving business results and you are looking for an opportunity with a dynamic, fast-paced organisation focusing on automations and scalability and be part of a distributed team, this could be a great fit. What You Will Be Doing: Drive monthly and quarterly close cycles for accruals, payments and general system updates in our Sales Incentive tool, Xactly Incent Responsible for SOX reviews, compliance and driving continuous improvement Find opportunities for system improvements and work closely with IT and key partners to implement technologies that enhance compensation processes Ensure accuracy and integrity of sales compensation data, applying Xactly and SalesForce data analysis and reporting tools to provide actionable insights Design, plan and perform user acceptance testing for annual compensation plan reset process or special projects by ensuring full accuracy of Xactly system calculation Document and communicate test results, and coordinate with IT, broader Sales Compensation team and other departments to address any issues Provide training and support to sales teams and other stakeholders on compensation plans, processes, and system changes. What You Bring: 5+ years experience in Sales Compensation / Operation / Analytics area (knowledge of sales compensation processes, year-end and month close activities) 3+ years experience with Xactly Incent and Analytics commission software or similar commission applications, plus a working experience with, Workday, ServiceNow Strong proficiency with Excel and attention to detail Confirmed experience in design and execution of complex user acceptance testing and system implementation projects Strong analytical and reasoning skills, good communication skills Thriving in fast pace environments and desire to own, re-build, improve upon existing processes and agile to changes Great teammate who can partner well across various departments and but also able to work independently and drive initiatives Additional Information - We Take Care of Our People: As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do. We strive to have parity of benefits across regions, and while regulations differ from place to place, we believe taking care of our people is the right thing to do. Competitive pay based on the work you do here and not your previous salary Health coverage for you and your family in many locations Ability to craft your calendar with flexible locations and schedules for many roles Generous number of vacation days each year Increase your impact - We match up to $2000 (or local currency equivalent) for financial donations and service Up to 40 hours each year to use toward volunteer projects you love Embracing parenthood with a minimum of 16 weeks of parental leave Different people approach problems differently. review_candidates.title: Payroll Support Specialist
review_candidates.description: MSA Asia is a China and Asia-Pacific business consultancy established in 2011. We help foreign companies register businesses, manage accounting and tax compliance, run payroll, and navigate financial advisory across China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Vietnam, Thailand, India, and Malaysia. We are building a diverse, international team and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, regardless of gender, ethnicity, nationality, religion, sexual orientation, family status, age, or disability. Position Overview MSA Asia is looking for a Payroll Support Specialist to assist companies that outsource the payroll administration of their Asian entities to us. Working remotely from Latin America, you will support client HR and finance teams with payroll calculations, employee payments, statutory deductions, employer contributions, reimbursements, and payroll-related billing. You will work closely with our accounting, payroll, and local compliance teams to ensure that payroll is processed accurately and in accordance with the requirements of each Asian jurisdiction. The role requires strong numerical accuracy, clear client communication, and the ability to investigate payroll discrepancies across different countries, currencies, and employment systems. Key Responsibilities Respond to payroll enquiries from client HR and finance teams concerning salaries, deductions, employer contributions, reimbursements, benefits, and payment dates. Support the monthly payroll process for companies operating their own legal entities across Asia. Review payroll inputs, including new hires, terminations, salary changes, bonuses, leave, expenses, and other employee adjustments. Reconcile gross-to-net payroll reports against funding requests, employee payment files, and client invoices. Investigate discrepancies involving payroll calculations, exchange rates, statutory deductions, employer costs, or employee payments. Coordinate with MSA Asia’s accounting, finance, and local payroll teams to resolve payroll issues and meet monthly processing deadlines. Provide clients with clear breakdowns of payroll costs and explanations of country-specific deductions and contributions. Maintain accurate records of payroll instructions, approvals, amendments, and completed payments. Help improve internal payroll procedures, reporting templates, and client communication processes. Key Qualifications Two to four or more years of experience in payroll administration, payroll support, accounting, billing, or a related finance role. Previous experience with outsourced payroll, accounting services, or multi-country payroll operations is preferred. A strong understanding of gross-to-net payroll calculations, statutory deductions, employer contributions, and payroll reconciliations. Experience reviewing payroll reports and identifying numerical or billing discrepancies. Familiarity with foreign-exchange calculations and payments involving multiple currencies. Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work accurately under recurring monthly deadlines. Strong written and spoken English. The ability to explain payroll and accounting matters clearly to clients who may not have specialist knowledge. A professional, organised, and service-oriented approach to client support. What It Is Like Working at MSA Asia Our services. MSA Asia is a company incorporation and accounting firm supporting international businesses throughout Asia. We help clients establish local entities and manage the practical requirements that follow, including bookkeeping, tax filings, payroll, corporate secretarial work, and ongoing compliance. Our international team. You will work remotely with colleagues, clients, accountants, and local specialists across multiple countries. The role offers exposure to different Asian payroll systems and the opportunity to develop a broad understanding of regional business operations. Our working environment. We value accuracy, accountability, practical problem-solving, and clear communication. Payroll is time-sensitive and directly affects employees, so we expect team members to take ownership of issues and follow them through to resolution. Benefits and Perks A competitive salary A remote working environment The opportunity to work with an international team Exposure to payroll and accounting requirements across Asia Professional development and internal growth opportunities Flexibility to work from abroad for short periods The necessary hardware and systems to perform the role effectively
